svg.aria-label: Wiring diagram of the leak-test (DM-TL) module with the M3 DME as BMW draws it, for a Touring and donor built from 09/2001, showing the pump-on-30 result of the test, and the test that decides pins 20 and 30. Fuse F3 (20 A, after the DME relay) feeds X6021 pin 2, 1.5 RT/WS, from the M3 harness to splice X11212, which also feeds the K96 and K19 relay coils, and on by a 0.75 RT/WS wire to module pin 4, +12 V. Inside the module the heater, valve and pump each run from pin 4 to their own pin. The M3 DME's X60004 pin 18 takes the 0.75 SW/RT heater wire to module pin 2; this wire is moved first: from body X6011 pin 7 on an MS43 Touring built from 09/2001, after which the clutch wire takes X6011 pin 7, or from X60004 pin 2 on an MS45.1, where pins 2 and 15 are both SW/RT and need tags. A Touring built before 09/2001 has a three-wire module and no heater wire: fit 16137193479 and run a new 0.75 mm2 wire from X60004 pin 18 to module pin 2. X60004 pin 20 (MSS54 name: valve, DMTL) goes to module pin 1 and pin 30 (pump, DMTLP) to module pin 3. The MS43 and MSS54 tables call pin 20 the valve and pin 30 the pump, the MS45.1 table the reverse, and every heated-module drawing wires 20 to module pin 1 and 30 to pin 3. MS45.1 and MSS54 drawings show 20 as 0.75 BR/BL and 30 as 0.5 SW/GN; the US MS43 drawing has the colors the other way round, as did one MS43 car, so go by the cavity, not the color or the name. After the engine swap, STEUERN_DMTL_HEIZUNG switches the heater, START_SYSTEMCHECK_DMTL then LESEN_SYSTEMCHECK_DMTL run the check, and the faults are 14 (0x0E) heater, 27 (0x1B) valve and 127 (0x7F) module. The test before you swap 20 and 30: first, with the Touring's DME still in, run its leak-test jobs (MS45.1, MS450DS0.PRG: STEUERN_DMTL_P, _V and _H; MS43, MS430DS0.PRG: STEUERN_DMTL_MOTOR, _VENTIL and _HEIZUNG) and tag the X60004 wire that switches for each, using a test lamp at the back of the plug; the MSS54 has no pump or valve job of its own. Second, with the heater in pin 18, DME unplugged and module plugged in (power-up step 9), measure X60004 pins 18 to 20, 18 to 30 and 20 to 30: each element is the two readings that include its pin, added, minus the third, divided by two, and the lowest is the pump; a new Bosch module (E93) read about 68, 52 and 44 ohms, giving heater 38, valve 30 and pump 14 ohms, generic values rather than BMW limits. Third, if still unsure, bench-check the module with 12 volts through a fused lead on its pin 4, grounding pin 1 and then pin 3; the pump should run on one and the valve click on the other, the manual's inference from the drawings. The MSS54 wants the pump on 30: pump on 30, change nothing; pump on 20, swap 20 and 30.
